public_rationale: OpenAI’s Sora launch demonstrations explicitly document spontaneous appearances of people or animals. Together with the earlier GPT-4V evaluation, the record supports the claim that multimodal systems retain fabrication errors and exhibit visual forms of failure. It does not establish that multimodal training fails to reduce errors.
limitations: The evidence establishes the existence of failures, not their prevalence across all multimodal systems.
The GPT-4V evaluation predates the target period and is context only.
New ways is interpreted as visual manifestations, not historical novelty.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Multimodal systems trained on text and images still hallucinate and make other errors, sometimes in new ways.

statement.excerpt: Nowadays, we have “multimodal” systems, trained on both text and images, and the aforementioned “hallucinations” (perhaps better called failed approximations, as Gerben Wierda has pointed out) and other errors persist and even crop up in new ways.

from_speaker: “multimodal” systems, trained on both text and images
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that adding visual training has not eliminated fabricated content or errors, and that visual systems exhibit additional forms of error.
This does not assert that every model fails, that error rates have not improved, or that multimodal training provides no benefit.
For this ongoing observation, I use the publication month through the post date. Model demonstrations and evaluations have no standard quarterly reporting period.
New ways means errors involving visual content or consistency, rather than a claim of historically unprecedented error categories.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous multimodal outputs or evaluations document fabricated content and visual errors despite training involving text and visual material.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The cited failures are shown to be misidentified, and reliable evaluations establish that the relevant contemporary multimodal systems no longer exhibit the claimed errors.
